# One-Line Answers — Last-Minute Revision

*Generated by `python scripts/build_viva.py` from the project's own
outputs. Every figure below is read from `outputs/tables/report_facts.json`,
the same fact pack used by the report and the presentation. The dataset is
synthetic and is described as such throughout.*

| Term | One-line answer |
| --- | --- |
| **Customer Revenue Intelligence** | Converting transaction records into customer-level understanding and forward-looking revenue decisions. |
| **RFM** | Scoring each customer 1–5 on Recency, Frequency and Monetary value to place them in a named segment. |
| **Recency** | Days since the customer's last delivered purchase, measured at 2026-01-01. |
| **Frequency** | Count of distinct orders with at least one delivered line. |
| **Monetary** | Total delivered sales value for that customer, after discount. |
| **CLV** | Customer lifetime value — here reported as measured historical profit and separately as estimated forward twelve-month profit. |
| **K-Means** | Unsupervised algorithm partitioning customers into K clusters by minimising within-cluster variance; K = 4 here. |
| **Centroid** | The mean position of a cluster's members in feature space. |
| **Silhouette** | How much closer a point is to its own cluster than to the nearest other; 0.3534 here. |
| **ARI** | Chance-corrected agreement between two partitions; 0.3952 between my RFM segments and clusters. |
| **PCA** | Projection into fewer dimensions; used here for visualisation only, 95.09% in two components. |
| **EDA** | Examining distributions, trends, relationships and outliers before modelling. |
| **Feature engineering** | Creating variables that carry business meaning; 28 added to the cleaned dataset. |
| **Revenue Prediction** | Supervised regression of a customer's delivered revenue in the next quarter; Linear regression, test R² 0.0557. |
| **Forecasting** | Projecting company monthly revenue forward from its own history; Theta: Theta (seasonality auto-tested), 6 months, 14.56% backtest MAPE. |
| **Prediction vs forecasting** | Prediction is per customer per quarter using customer features; forecasting is one company series over time. |
| **MAE** | Mean absolute error, same unit as the target; ₹5,658 on prediction. |
| **RMSE** | Root mean squared error; penalises large misses more; ₹11,232. |
| **R²** | Share of variance explained relative to predicting the mean; 0.0557. |
| **MAPE** | Mean absolute percentage error; unusable near zero actuals; 7.77% on the forecast test split. |
| **WAPE** | Weighted absolute percentage error; used where actuals hit zero; 127.83%. |
| **Spearman ρ** | Rank correlation; 0.4869 for the customer-value model. |
| **SQL** | Language for querying relational data; 11 tables, 57 queries, all 56 checks passing. |
| **Window function** | Computes across related rows without collapsing them; used in 35 project queries. |
| **CTE** | A named temporary result defined with `WITH`; used in 27 queries. |
| **Power BI** | Microsoft BI tool; star schema of 13 tables with 84 DAX measures. |
| **DAX** | Power BI's formula language, evaluated within filter context. |
| **Measure vs calculated column** | A measure computes at query time in filter context; a column is computed and stored at refresh. |
| **Star schema** | One central fact table surrounded by dimension tables. |
| **Streamlit** | Python framework for data applications; 12 pages, 40/40 tests passing. |
| **Dashboard vs application** | A dashboard presents pre-computed measures; an application executes logic and loads real models. |
| **Data leakage** | Using information at training time that would not exist at prediction time. |
| **Temporal leakage** | Training on periods that come after the test period; avoided with a chronological split. |
| **Overfitting** | Fitting training noise so the score does not survive unseen data. |
| **Underfitting** | A model too simple to capture the available signal. |
| **Backtesting** | Rolling-origin time-series validation; 7 folds here. |
| **Stationarity** | Statistical properties constant over time; ADF p = 0.2015, so not stationary in level. |
| **Prediction interval** | The range a future observation is expected to fall in; 80% = ₹1.00 Cr to ₹2.16 Cr. |
| **Delivered revenue** | The project's one revenue rule — delivered order lines only, in Python, SQL and DAX alike. |
| **Inactivity (not churn)** | Recency-based flag; the dataset defines no churn event, so the word churn never describes a result. |
